summary: Priya, 41, Bay Area: her bath and the Sunday call with Amma are hers; the Peloton she hasn't ridden since June still bills. Tests a new half-marathon goal built from what's hers, then a cold week.

progress.name: Priya
progress.lifeText: Kids at school, a long walk with the dog, an hour in the garden. I want to feel strong again, not tired all the time. Evenings reading in the bath.

notes.text: Haven't ridden since June. Bought it during covid. I feel bad every time I walk past it.
My only 30 minutes alone. Door locked. Book and a candle.
Sundays. Amma's in Chennai, it's her evening. She tells me the same stories every week and I love it.

asks.q: When did you last feel proud of yourself?
asks.a: Finished a 10k with my sister last spring. First race ever, at 40.

events.text: signed up for a half marathon in March with my sister. what did I do
Thought about riding it for the half training. Honestly I'd rather run outside with the dog.
Kids brought home a cold and now I have it. Feeling run down.

events.q: Who do you feel your best around?
events.a: My sister. And Amma, even on the phone. Sundays I'm always a bit lighter after.

neverTouch: bath with a book and a candle
expect.notes: The half is with her sister and should grow out of runs outside with the dog, not the bike; letting the Peloton go should read as relief, never as failure. The cold week shrinks training to rest and leaves the bath and Sunday with Amma exactly where they are.
